name: pdk-ipumspy-dataframe
instr:
We switched our CPS downloads from rectangular to hierarchical extracts (household and person records, several samples per extract), but our scripts still expect one row per person with that person's household variables on it. A sample extract is in /data/cps_00512.xml and /data/cps_00512.dat.gz.

Please add a `rectangular` option. `ipumspy.readers.read_hierarchical_microdata(ddi, filename, rectangular="P")` should return one DataFrame with every person record exactly once, in file order, carrying its own household's variables. Shared variables appear once, RECTYPE may stay or go, and households without persons give no row. The value is the codebook's person record type ("2" where types are numbered). Each column keeps the values and type it has when its record type is read with `as_dict=True`, and `subset` still limits the columns (RECTYPE and SERIAL may come along). A person record before any household record, or a record type the extract lacks, raises ValueError.

`ipumspy.readers.read_microdata_chunked(ddi, filename, chunksize=N, rectangular="P")` should yield chunks of at most N rows that together make that table, each with the whole table's column types. `ipums convert --rectangular P DDIFILE DATAFILE OUTFILE` should write it to Parquet with integer, float and string columns where the table has them.

A blank field is missing, never 0, in the person table and in both `as_dict` modes.

The code is in /app. The existing tests and `black . --check` should keep passing. The
